 Seoul shares open lower on Democratic Party victory in US midterm elections
 Published : Nov. 5, 2026 - 09:19:34
 Add The Korea Herald on Google
 Link copied!
 Financial data is displayed on a screen at the dealing room of Hana Bank in central Seoul on Nov. 4, 2026. (Yonhap) South Korean stocks started lower Thursday as the U.S. midterm elections ended with a Democratic Party victory, raising concerns over tighter artificial intelligence regulations.
 The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index fell 103.71 points, or 1.82 percent, to 5,580.09 at the opening bell.
 US stocks finished higher as the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 3 percent, and the S&P 500 gained 1.6 percent. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite added 1.4 percent.
 However, the PHLX chip index fell 3.1 percent to hit a six-month low as investors were concerned about stricter regulations on AI data centers by the new Democrats-led Congress. (Yonhap)
